nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a biunitary triperfect number, that is, a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum. If the exact power of $2$ dividing $N$ is $2^4$ and the exact power of $3$ dividing $N$ is $3^3$ or $3^4$, then $N = 2160$.
nodes.title: Biunitary triperfect numbers exactly divisible by $2^4$ and by $3^3$ or $3^4$

nodes.summary: For every integer $g \ge 1$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(41^g)$ has a prime factor $q$ with $q \notin \{2, 3, 5, 13\}$.
nodes.title: Prime factors of the biunitary divisor sum of $41^g$

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every integer $g \ge 2$ with $(p, g) \ne (2, 4)$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(p^g)$ has a prime factor $q \ge 5$.
nodes.title: Prime factors at least $5$ of biunitary divisor sums of prime powers

nodes.summary: For every odd prime $p$ and every integer $g \ge 4$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(p^g)$ has a prime factor $q \ge 7$.
nodes.title: Prime factors at least $7$ of biunitary divisor sums of odd prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ be integers with $(a, n) \ne (2, 3)$, and if $n = 1$ suppose that $a + 1$ is not a power of $2$. Then $a^n + 1$ has a primitive prime factor $p$, that is, a prime $p$ that divides $a^n + 1$ but divides no $a^m + 1$ with $1 \le m < n$, such that $p \equiv 1 \pmod{2n}$.
nodes.title: Primitive prime factors of $a^n + 1$

nodes.summary: For every integer $g \ge 2$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(13^g)$ has two distinct prime factors $q_1$ and $q_2$, neither of which lies in $\{2, 3, 41, 547\}$.
nodes.title: Two prime factors of the biunitary divisor sum of $13^g$

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a biunitary triperfect number, that is, a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum. If $3^3$ divides $N$, then the exact power of $2$ dividing $N$ is not $2^5$.
nodes.title: No biunitary triperfect number divisible by $27$ is exactly divisible by $2^5$

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a biunitary triperfect number, that is, a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum. If $3^3$ divides $N$, then the exact power of $2$ dividing $N$ is not $2^6$.
nodes.title: No biunitary triperfect number divisible by $27$ is exactly divisible by $2^6$

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a biunitary triperfect number, that is, a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum. If $3^3$ divides $N$, then $2^4$ divides $N$.
nodes.title: Biunitary triperfect numbers divisible by $27$ are divisible by $16$

nodes.summary: Biunitary triperfect numbers exactly divisible by $2^4$ and divisible by $3^5$ are prime to $5$. Let $N$ be a biunitary triperfect number, that is, a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum. If the exact power of $2$ dividing $N$ is $2^4$ and $3^5$ divides $N$, then $5$ does not divide $N$.
nodes.title: Biunitary triperfect numbers exactly divisible by $2^4$ and divisible by $3^5$ are prime to $5$

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum, and let $e$ and $f$ be the exponents of $2$ and $3$ in the prime factorization of $N$. If $f \ge 3$, then $e \ge 7$ and $f = 4$ do not both hold.
nodes.title: No biunitary triperfect number has $3$-exponent $4$ and $2$-exponent at least $7$

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a positive integer with $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum, and let $e$ and $f$ be the exponents of $2$ and $3$ in the prime factorization of $N$. If $f \ge 3$, then $e \ge 7$ and $f = 3$ do not both hold.
nodes.title: No biunitary triperfect number has $3$-exponent $3$ and $2$-exponent at least $7$

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(n)$ is odd if and only if $n = 2^k$ for some natural number $k$ (so $n = 1$ is included).
nodes.title: Parity of the biunitary divisor sum

nodes.summary: Let $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ be a primitive prime divisor of the integer sequence $m \mapsto a^m - 1$ at index $n$, that is, a prime that divides $a^n - 1$ and divides no $a^m - 1$ with $1 \le m < n$. Then $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$.
nodes.title: Primitive prime divisors of $a^n - 1$ are $1$ modulo $n$

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $N$ divisible by $27$, $\sigma^{**}(N) = 3N$ if and only if $N = 2160$, where $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum.
nodes.title: The only biunitary triperfect number divisible by $27$ is $2160$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $m \ge 1$ and $e \ge 2m - 1$ be natural numbers, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. Then, in $\mathbb{Q}$, $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge \sigma^{**}(p^{2m})/p^{2m}$, and if moreover $e \ne 2m$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge \sum_{i=0}^{m} 1/p^i$.
nodes.title: Comparison bounds for the biunitary divisor sum of a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $e \ge 1$, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. Then, in $\mathbb{Q}$, $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge 1 + 1/p^2$; if moreover $e \ne 2$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge 1 + 1/p$; and if $e \ge 3$, then $\sigma^{**}(p^e)/p^e \ge (1 + 1/p)(1 + 1/p^3)$.
nodes.title: Lower bounds for the biunitary divisor sum of a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $f$, $t$ and $\eta$ be natural numbers with $\eta \in \{0, 1\}$ and $f = 2t - 1 - \eta$, suppose $f \ge 5$, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. nodes.title: Prime factors of the biunitary divisor sum of a power of $3$

nodes.summary: Let $e$, $s$ and $\delta$ be natural numbers with $\delta \in \{0, 1\}$ and $e = 2s - 1 - \delta$, suppose $e \ge 6$ and $e \notin \{8, 12\}$, and write $\sigma^{**}$ for the biunitary divisor sum. Then at least one of the following holds: (a) $\delta = 0$ and $\sigma^{**}(2^e)$ has two distinct prime factors $q_1, q_2$ with $5 < q_i \le 2^s - 1$ for $i = 1, 2$; (b) $5 \mid \sigma^{**}(2^e)$; (c) $\sigma^{**}(2^e)$…
nodes.title: Prime factors of the biunitary divisor sum of a power of $2$

nodes.summary: For every odd natural number $n$, $2^{\omega(n)}$ divides $\sigma^{**}(n)$, where $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ and $\sigma^{**}$ is the biunitary divisor sum.
nodes.title: Powers of two dividing the biunitary divisor sum of an odd number

nodes.summary: For every positive even natural number $n$, writing $\omega(n)$ for the number of distinct prime factors of $n$, the power $2^{\omega(n) - 1}$ divides the biunitary divisor sum $\sigma^{**}(n)$.
nodes.title: Divisibility of the biunitary divisor sum of an even number by a power of two

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
